summary: Reviewed test_tool_wrappers.py (Python) and pipeline.test.ts (TypeScript) for WP-005.

All 5 acceptance criteria are confirmed met. All TestRestrictToWp* classes are present in test_tool_wrappers.py and cover the full behavioural surface: importability, empty-wp-id no-op, matching pass-through, mismatch ValueError (flat-dict + ToolCall structure), idempotency (no double-wrapping, guard still fires), chained composition with inject_project_path, and create_stage_node integration.

The TS handoff_notes bare-string coercion test is present in pipeline.test.ts (line 1132) and is accompanied by 3 additional companion tests (string[] preserved, omit → no entry, schema-level bare-string acceptance). This is comprehensive and goes beyond the minimum AC.

Test design quality is high: use of `_make_guard_tool()` / `_make_stage_node_state()` helpers avoids repetition; parametric WP IDs (ACTIVE_WP constant) improve readability; the `patch()` strategy in TestRestrictToWpInCreateStageNode correctly patches at the module import level (`src.nodes.restrict_to_wp`) rather than at the source definition level.
No imports of non-existent symbols — all imports resolve against actual WP-002/WP-003 deliverables.
506 Python tests pass; 108 TS pipeline tests pass. No regressions.

comments.note: test_tool_wrappers.py: TestRestrictToWpInCreateStageNode correctly patches `src.nodes.restrict_to_wp` (import-level), not `src.utils.tool_wrappers.restrict_to_wp`. This is the right approach and ensures the patch intercepts the actual call in create_stage_node. Worth noting as a good pattern for future node integration tests.

pipeline.test.ts: the `as any` cast on line 1140 (`handoff_notes: 'Please check the auth module' as any`) is intentional — it bypasses the TS type system to test the JS-layer normalization. The comment above makes the intent clear. Consider adding an inline comment like `// bypasses TS types to test runtime normalization` directly on the cast line for future maintainers.

No test asserts that `restrict_to_wp` is called AFTER `inject_project_path` within `create_stage_node` (ordering). The chained integration test (TestRestrictToWpIntegrationWithInjectProjectPath) verifies correctness of composition but does not enforce the order. This is a very low-priority gap — the current implementation order is visible in __init__.py and both orderings produce correct results in the current guard logic.
